articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces further highlights of its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Announces Further Highlights for 2026 Miami Beach Edition
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach announces new gallery presentations, the complete Conversations program, and Zero 10 initiatives for its upcoming edition featuring 272 exhibitors.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach released further details for its 2026 edition, convening 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories. The event, whose Global Lead Partner is UBS, takes place from December 4 to 6, 2026, at the Miami Beach Convention Center, with VIP previews on December 2 and 3. The showfloor features a reconfigured layout shaped by feedback from exhibitors, collectors, and the Selection Committee. The Galleries sector brings programs from the Americas, Latin America, and the Caribbean into dialogue with participants from Europe, Asia, and beyond. Mendes Wood DM presents Rosana Paulino's bronze sculpture, while Gladstone features works by Wangechi Mutu and Carrie Mae Weems. David Kordansky Gallery exhibits pieces by Rashid Johnson and Shara Hughes. Mariane Ibrahim explores memory and inherited histories through works by Lorraine O'Grady and Clotilde Jiménez. Spinello Projects marks its twentieth anniversary, and Ortuzar and Crèvecœur present a joint booth. OMR showcases international artists exploring nature and materiality, while the Zero 10 program returns to Miami Beach for digital era art.

articles.originalTitle: At the Broad, Six Decades of Art Question the Myth of Progress - ARTnews.com
articles.title: The Broad in Los Angeles Examines the Myth of Progress
articles.excerpt: A new exhibition at The Broad in Los Angeles brings together six decades of artwork to examine media representation and sociopolitical events.
articles.content: A new exhibition at The Broad in Los Angeles examines how media shapes public perception of major sociopolitical events through works spanning six decades. Organized by assistant curator Jen Vanegas Rocha, the presentation brings together creations by more than a dozen artists, including Andy Warhol, Barbara Kruger, Glenn Ligon, and Guadalupe Rosales. The exhibition shares its title with Rosales's 2024 sculpture, which encases a yellowed 1992 Los Angeles newspaper within an aluminum frame and two-way mirror. Founding director Joanne Heyler noted that the presentation reflects a growing difficulty in believing that change unfolds in a dependable, escalating linear progression. The oldest piece in the presentation, Andy Warhol's 1963 Race Riot, depicts police dogs attacking civil rights demonstrators in Alabama. Artist Hank Willis Thomas observed that such works function as postcards to the future. The exhibition highlights numerous recent acquisitions, showcasing artists unrepresented in the institution's collection previously as part of an ongoing effort to reflect diverse community histories.

articles.originalTitle: Hoor Al Qasimi to curate Venice Biennale in 2028 - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Hoor Al Qasimi Appointed Curator of the 2028 Venice Biennale
articles.excerpt: The director of the Sharjah Art Foundation and the Sharjah Biennial, Hoor Al Qasimi, has been appointed curator of the 62nd International Art Exhibition, marking the second consecutive edition with a woman from outside the Western art world.
articles.content: Hoor Al Qasimi, one of the preeminent figures of contemporary art in the Middle East, has been named curator of the Venice Biennale's next art exhibition. Following this year's edition curated by the late Koyo Kouoh, the appointment of Al Qasimi from the UAE marks the second consecutive edition in which a woman from outside the Western art world has been chosen for the role. Born into the royal family of Sharjah, Al Qasimi curated the sixth edition of the Sharjah Biennial in 2003 after completing her undergraduate studies at the Slade School of Fine Art in London. In 2009, she founded the Sharjah Art Foundation, a public art organisation promoting contemporary art collaborations internationally. She holds board positions for numerous arts organisations, including the International Biennial Association and Sharjah Museums Authority, and has curated major exhibitions such as the Lahore Biennale in 2020, the Aichi Triennale in 2025, and this year's Biennale of Sydney. Venice Biennale president Pietrangelo Buttafuoco stated that Al Qasimi's work brings together attentiveness to deep-rooted memory and its legacies. Al Qasimi stated that she was honoured to be appointed as curator.

articles.originalTitle: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires – exhibition large print guide - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Constantinople to Istanbul: Exhibition Explores the Legacy of Two Empires
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum explores the rich artistic heritage of the Roman and Ottoman periods through a new exhibition.
articles.content: Originally designated as Nova Roma by Emperor Constantine I in 330 CE, the ancient city developed into the capital of two successive empires before falling in 1453 and later flourishing under Ottoman rule until 1922. Positioned at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, the metropolis thrived through maritime trade, taxation, and imperial patronage. A new exhibition guide published by the Victoria and Albert Museum examines the urban fabric, monumental architecture, and diverse artistic traditions that defined the city across sixteen centuries. Key engineering feats, including the 5.6 km long Theodosian Walls and the Aqueduct of Valens, ensured the security and sustenance of the capital during peace and siege. The display highlights contrasting visual cultures, ranging from Byzantine sacred imagery such as Christ Pantocrator to Ottoman calligraphy and literary reverence. Artefacts featured in the exhibition include carved ivories, restoration inscriptions, archaeological photographs by K.A.C. Creswell, and personal devotional objects like precious gemstone cameos and pectoral crosses. These items reflect the complex interplay of classical heritage, Christian protection, and imperial authority that sustained the city throughout its long history.

articles.originalTitle: Tate Liverpool Plans Fall 2027 Reopening With Surrealism Survey - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Tate Liverpool Plans Fall 2027 Reopening With Surrealism Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Following a £30 million transformation, Tate Liverpool will reopen in fall 2027 with an exhibition featuring works by Salvador Dalí, Eileen Agar, and Man Ray.
articles.content: Tate Liverpool is preparing to reopen in fall 2027 after undergoing a £30 million transformation of its home inside an 1846 warehouse on the Royal Albert Dock. The gallery will mark its reopening with the exhibition “Surrealism: Staging Dream Worlds,” echoing the institution's inaugural surrealist show held in 1988. Scheduled to run from fall 2027 through spring 2028, the exhibition will present works by artists such as Salvador Dalí, Eileen Agar, and Man Ray. According to Tate Liverpool, the showcase will additionally explore the movement's significant role in theater and dance history through major stage set and costume commissions. Visitors will also be able to view Dorothea Tanning's costume designs for the ballet The Witch, photographs documenting Sheila Legge's performance at the 1936 International Surrealist Exhibition in London, and archival materials from Ted Joans. The gallery originally closed in October 2023 with a planned reopening for 2025, but fundraising challenges pushed the schedule back. Architectural redesign of the building is being handled by 6a architects as part of an overall £35 million renovation effort.

articles.originalTitle: The Critic as Artist (And Vice Versa): A Fireside Chat with Jerry Saltz - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Critic Jerry Saltz Discusses Career During Art Week NYC
articles.excerpt: New York magazine senior art critic Jerry Saltz shared his perspectives on art criticism, social media, and auctions during an event held as part of Art Week NYC.
articles.content: New York magazine senior art critic Jerry Saltz participated in a fireside chat at the PMC Studio in Midtown Manhattan during the Art Week NYC festival, which is organized by ARTnews, Artforum, and Art in America. During the event, Saltz discussed how he became a critic, his prominence on social media, and his thoughts on contemporary art production. Maintaining his skepticism toward artificial intelligence, the critic also expressed his strong aversion to auctions. Offering advice to creative individuals, Saltz touched upon a recent documentary featuring him and his wife, former New York Times chief art critic Roberta Smith. Despite various challenges, Saltz expressed his ongoing belief in New York City as a vital community center for artists during the well-attended session with the audience.

articles.originalTitle: Desai Chia designs Bethesda Residence to balance “openness and discretion” - Dezeen
articles.title: Desai Chia Architecture Designs Bethesda Residence Balancing Openness and Discretion
articles.excerpt: Designed for a tight site in Maryland by New York-based Desai Chia Architecture, the Bethesda Residence balances privacy concerns with openness through a vertical light well that brings daylight deep into the home.
articles.content: New York-based Desai Chia Architecture designed a three-level private residence on a tight site in Bethesda, Maryland. Because neighbouring houses are close together, the architects focused on balancing openness and discretion. The rectangular building features grey fibre-cement panel cladding and a modern bay window on both the front and rear facades. Public spaces occupy the ground level, while the upper levels contain bedrooms and two offices, with a rooftop terrace on the top floor. The basement holds a gym, ping-pong area and media room. To provide natural illumination, the team positioned a three-storey light well along the central staircase. The all-electric house features a geothermal heating and cooling system and includes a shaft for a potential future ADA-compliant elevator. The project was designed by Desai Chia Architecture with Thomson & Cooke Architects serving as the architect of record.

articles.originalTitle: Project Domani Public Consultation - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery in London Launches Public Consultation for New Wing
articles.excerpt: The National Gallery in London has initiated a public consultation for a planned new wing at the St Vincent House site. Feedback is open until 23 December 2026.
articles.content: The National Gallery has released emerging proposals for a new wing located on the site of St Vincent House behind the Sainsbury Wing. Entitled Project Domani, the initiative aims to expand permanent display spaces, improve connections across the estate, and enhance surrounding public spaces. The proposals would provide approximately 6,000 square meters of gallery and exhibition space, allowing the history of Western painting from the 13th century to the present to be presented as a continuous journey. Developed by architect Kengo Kuma alongside other partners, the design includes pedestrian route improvements between Trafalgar Square and Leicester Square, as well as a landscaped public roof garden. Gallery Director Sir Gabriele Finaldi noted that the new wing will extend the institution's collection into the 20th and 21st centuries. The public consultation remains open until 23 December 2026, with feedback informing more detailed proposals expected in Spring 2027.

articles.originalTitle: 18th Biennale de Lyon: A Poetic Economy? - ArtReview
articles.title: Lyon Biennale Explores Exchange and Poetic Economy
articles.excerpt: Curated by Catherine Nichols, the 18th Biennale de Lyon takes Robert Filliou's concept of a poetic economy as its starting point, examining exchange, circulation, and urban passages across multiple venues.
articles.content: Spread across three main venues in Lyon, the 18th Biennale de Lyon takes inspiration from Robert Filliou's poetic economy concept, which extends exchange beyond material goods to ideas and collective life. Australian-born curator Catherine Nichols anchors this framework through the metaphor of Lyon's traboules passageways. At Les Grandes Locos, a former train-maintenance warehouse, the exhibition focuses on industrialisation, labour, and materials, featuring works by artists such as Laure Prouvost, Selma Selman, Joël Andrianomearisoa, and Lara Almarcegui. Across the three floors of macLYON, colonial histories and their legacies come to the foreground, featuring creations by Thu-Van Tran and Sara Sejin Chang. Luke Willis Thompson's film trilogy addressing Oceania and domestic-focused installations at the Musée des Tissus further contribute to the extensive programme. The sprawling exhibition brings together a diverse array of works exploring exchange, collective creation, and the legacies of history across multiple sites.

articles.originalTitle: Are trees on buildings more than a greenwashing gimmick? - Dezeen
articles.title: Are Trees on Buildings an Architectural Solution or Greenwashing?
articles.excerpt: The rising global trend of tree-covered buildings has divided the architectural world over carbon costs, biodiversity, and structural challenges.
articles.content: Over the past decade, buildings featuring trees have sprouted globally in cities such as New York, Paris, Shanghai, and Sydney, becoming a defining architectural trend. While studios like BIG, MVRDV, MAD, and Ateliers Jean Nouvel have embraced this approach, nearly every project triggers accusations of greenwashing. Fernando Scherner of Buro Happold notes that vegetation on buildings supports biodiversity and provides natural cooling through shade and evapotranspiration, reducing air conditioning needs. However, critics argue that the extra structural steel and concrete required to support trees and soil generate upfront carbon emissions that far outweigh what the trees can sequester. Carolina Montano Owen of the World Green Building Council points out that trees sequester carbon relatively slowly compared to these upfront manufacturing costs. While projects like Milan's Bosco Verticale achieved international acclaim, others like Sydney's One Central Park and China's Qiyi City Forest Garden faced severe maintenance issues, falling planters, and pest infestations. Experts emphasize that such arboreal architecture demands rigorous multidisciplinary collaboration, botanical expertise, and case-by-case feasibility assessments rather than acting as a mere aesthetic decoration.

articles.originalTitle: kanal-centre pompidou opens in brussels inside restored 1930s citroën garage - Designboom
articles.title: Former Citroen Garage in Brussels Transformed into Cultural Center
articles.excerpt: Located along the Charleroi-Brussels Canal, a former Citroen garage has been transformed by Atelier Kanal into a 40,000-square-meter museum and cultural center opening in partnership with the Centre Pompidou.
articles.content: Built in 1933 and 1934 along the banks of the Charleroi-Brussels Canal, the former Citroen complex has been transformed by the Atelier Kanal consortium into a 40,000-square-meter museum and public cultural center. Opening on November 28, 2026, Kanal houses contemporary art, architecture, performance, film, and community activities under one roof, with over 20,000 square meters of freely accessible public space. The design team restored the existing industrial building and introduced three new structures within it. The museum's artistic program develops through a partnership with the Centre Pompidou, providing access to modern and contemporary art collections. The opening exhibition brings together more than 350 works dating from the early 20th century to today. Kanal Architecture, formerly known as CIVA, is also housed in the institution with its own library and research center. The public program features a 700-square-meter indoor playground designed by Assemble, alongside workshops, a research center, and community spaces.

articles.originalTitle: Visitors’ Lions of the Biennale Arte 2026 - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Visitors' Lions of the 2026 Venice Biennale Awarded to Nick Cave and India
articles.excerpt: The 2026 Visitors' Lions awards of the Venice Biennale, determined by public voting, have been presented to exhibition participant Nick Cave and the Pavilion of India.
articles.content: La Biennale di Venezia has announced the winners of the Visitors' Lions for the 61st International Art Exhibition, based on votes cast by ticket-holding visitors. The best participant award went to Chicago-born artist Nick Cave, featured in the exhibition curated by Koyo Kouoh. The best national participation was awarded to the Pavilion of India, curated by Amin Jaffer and commissioned by the National Gallery of Modern Art under the Ministry of Culture. Hosted at the Arsenale, the Indian pavilion featured artists Alwar Balasubramaniam, Sumakshi Singh, Ranjani Shettar, Asim Waqif, and Skarma Sonam Tashi. Visitors who toured both the Giardini and Arsenale venues between 9 May and 22 November were eligible to vote. Biennale President Pietrangelo Buttafuoco noted that the exhibition thrives on the vibrant presence of its public.

articles.originalTitle: “Intensely physical patterns” cloak Gerhard Richter’s self-designed gallery in Doha - Dezeen
articles.title: Artist Gerhard Richter Opens Hexagonal Gallery Pavilion in Doha
articles.excerpt: Built in MIA Park through a collaboration between artist Gerhard Richter and Selldorf Architects, the Doha Pavilion features vibrant tiles inspired by Richter's Strip paintings.
articles.content: Located in MIA Park in Doha, the Doha Pavilion was conceived as a permanent public structure and gallery space designed by artist Gerhard Richter in collaboration with US studio Selldorf Architects. Featuring a six-sided hexagonal form, the pavilion is wrapped in psychedelic, kaleidoscopic tiles that recall geometric patterns found in Islamic art, nodding to Richter's Strip painting series. Richter noted that his 2013 visit to the city sparked the idea for a structure uniting the themes of that body of work. Architect Annabelle Selldorf described the design as a profound culmination of the artist's years of research into abstraction. Inside the gallery, visitors can view archival works alongside new pieces created specifically for the pavilion, including a freestanding tripartite sculpture titled the Strip Tower. The opening of the Doha Pavilion coincides with the inaugural edition of the Rubaiya Qatar 2026 international visual arts quadrennial.

articles.originalTitle: can le corbusier’s last building be disassembled and shipped? - Designboom
articles.title: Can Le Corbusier's Last Building in Zurich Be Disassembled and Shipped?
articles.excerpt: French-Swiss architect Le Corbusier's final glass and steel building on Lake Zurich, Pavillon Le Corbusier, remains anchored to its original site by concrete stairs and a ramp, despite rumors regarding its prefabricated design and potential disassembly.
articles.content: Situated on the shores of Lake Zurich, the Pavillon Le Corbusier is the final completed building by the French-Swiss architect. Constructed from glass and steel, it is his only building built in this format. Following a 50-year land lease agreement initiated by gallerist Heidi Weber, the pavilion opened in 1967. Designed around prefabricated principles, the building was assembled on site using approximately 22,000 screws and modular units. After the half-century land lease period came to a close, popular rumors circulated in the city suggesting that Weber attempted to dismantle and relocate the building alongside interior furnishings due to its prefabricated appearance. However, according to Christian Brändle, director of the Museum für Gestaltung Zürich, unscrewing and rebuilding the structure elsewhere is technically impossible because its staircase and ramp are made of concrete. Managed since 2019 as part of the Zurich Design Museum following major restoration work, the building remains anchored to its original lakeside plot.

articles.originalTitle: Does Your Building Work or Does It Just Photograph Well? What Neuroscience and Use Data Could Teach Architects - ArchDaily
articles.title: An Examination of Real Usage Data and Neuroarchitecture in Design
articles.excerpt: Research shows that the physical experience of buildings often diverges from design expectations. Neuroarchitecture and usage data offer architects new methods to evaluate real-world building performance and human perception.
articles.content: The perception of buildings initially through digital models and social media visuals continues to influence design practices. Research by Ann Sussman and Justin Hollander into cognitive architecture reveals that human eyes tend to skip blank facades while lingering on details, contrast, and activity. Similarly, Anjan Chatterjee's laboratory notes that spatial experience is structured around coherence, fascination, and hominess. However, experts observe that architects frequently formulate predictions on building functionality without routinely collecting post-occupancy data. Researchers at the Technical University of Denmark highlight performance gaps between anticipated and actual occupancy rates. Although building information modeling software records architectural intent, integrating empirical usage metrics such as temperature, daylight, noise, and actual density remains uncommon. Physical discrepancies, such as the slippery glass steps on Venice's Ponte della Costituzione bridge during rain, illustrate the persistent gap between visual documentation and practical application. Future architectural approaches may increasingly depend on returning to completed projects to measure actual building performance and inhabitant interaction.

articles.originalTitle: A first look at Burberry’s Christmas tree for London’s V&A Museum, which features a collaboration with artist Ann Carrington - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Burberry Unveils Christmas Tree Collaboration at the V&A Museum in London
articles.excerpt: London's Victoria and Albert Museum unveiled a Christmas tree conceived by Burberry creative director Daniel Lee and artist Ann Carrington, marking the museum's 172nd anniversary.
articles.content: London's Victoria and Albert Museum introduced a festive Christmas tree installation in its grand entrance hall, conceived through a collaboration between Burberry creative director Daniel Lee and British artist Ann Carrington. The project coincides with the heritage fashion house's 170th anniversary celebrations and the museum's 172nd year. Carrington, known for sculptures utilizing found objects, constructed a 16ft-foot sculpture incorporating everyday items such as tin cans, cutlery, plates and money boxes into ribbons and rosettes. V&A director Tristram Hunt noted that the installation invites visitors to observe familiar materials in unexpected ways. Concurrently, the exhibition titled 'The Burberry Trench: Crafting an Icon', which traces the history of the brand's iconic trench coat, remains open to the public in the Prince Consort Gallery until January 3, 2027.

articles.originalTitle: The Biennale Arte 2026 by Koyo Kouoh closes on a high note, with 714,015 visitors - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: 61st International Art Exhibition in Venice Closes With 714,015 Visitors
articles.excerpt: The Biennale Arte 2026, curated by Koyo Kouoh, concluded with 714,015 visitors and a record 100 National Participations, despite running three weeks shorter than previous editions.
articles.content: The 61st International Art Exhibition, titled In Minor Keys and curated by Koyo Kouoh, closed on November 22, 2026, following events at the Arsenale. The exhibition welcomed 714,015 visitors, including 29,387 during the pre-opening, and featured a record 100 National Participations. Running for three weeks less than previous editions to accommodate the renovation of the Central Pavilion at the Giardini funded by the Ministry of Culture, the exhibition opened on May 9. President Pietrangelo Buttafuoco and Kouoh's team reflected on the success of the edition following its conclusion. The exhibition drew 3,831 accredited journalists during the preview days alone and generated over 5,500 articles in global media coverage. Educational activities engaged 73,264 participants, and the Biennale Sessions project involved 4,102 university students from 103 institutions. La Biennale di Venezia continues its environmental sustainability commitments into 2026, aiming to certify the carbon neutrality of its events in compliance with standards and offsetting emissions through certified carbon credits.

articles.originalTitle: Poliform and Yabu Pushelberg brought a dreamlike design experience to Shanghai - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Poliform and Yabu Pushelberg Present Immersive Solstice Exhibition in Shanghai
articles.excerpt: Italian furniture manufacturer Poliform and design duo Yabu Pushelberg showcased their immersive installation Solstice, inspired by the cyclical rhythm of nature, at Shanghai's Yard 200 in November.
articles.content: Italian furniture manufacturer Poliform and design studio Yabu Pushelberg presented their immersive installation Solstice at Shanghai's Yard 200 in November. Inspired by the cyclical rhythm of nature, the exhibition invited visitors to observe transitions between seasons through changing landscapes accessed via mirrored walls in an exterior garden. A winter-evoking room featured a mirrored glacier-like floor surrounding Aqualuna armchairs, while the main gallery introduced the Lanai bed system among green florals. Summer was represented by armchairs positioned on a reflective water surface, and a private VIP lounge brought autumn to life with earth-toned materials. This exhibition marked a continuation of the partnership between the Italian brand and the design studio following its introduction at Milan Design Week 2026. Poliform CEO Marco Spinelli noted that the Shanghai market is one of the most important and fast-growing for high-end design.

articles.originalTitle: Morning Pages: James Cahill reads from 'The Beverly Hills Housewife' | Events - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Author James Cahill to Read at the National Gallery in London
articles.excerpt: Author, critic and art historian James Cahill will read from his latest book on David Hockney during the second event of the Morning Pages series.
articles.content: Author, critic and art historian Dr. James Cahill will appear as a guest for the second installment of the Morning Pages series at the National Gallery in London. During the special gathering in the Supporters' House Salon, Cahill will discuss and read from his book titled 'The Beverly Hills Housewife: Hockney's Californian Muse and the World Beyond the Pool', published by Thames & Hudson. The event offers attendees an opportunity to gain insight directly from the author regarding David Hockney's world and artistic legacy. The reading will be followed by a question-and-answer session, along with an opportunity to purchase and have copies signed by the author. Based between London and Los Angeles, Cahill's previous literary works include his debut novel 'Tiepolo Blue', shortlisted for the Author's Club Best First Novel Award, and his second novel 'The Violet Health'. He also contributes articles to publications including Artforum, the Burlington Magazine, the Financial Times, the Los Angeles Times, the Spectator and the Times Literary Supplement.

articles.originalTitle: Lunchtime Lectures: Redesigning the Rosalinde and Arthur Gilbert Galleries: New Stories for a celebrated collection - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Hosts Lecture on the Redesign and Curatorial Approach of the Gilbert Galleries
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a lunchtime lecture on the design of the Rosalinde and Arthur Gilbert Galleries, which reopened in March 2026. Alice Minter and Jessica Insley will share new narratives of the collection.
articles.content: V&A South Kensington in London is hosting a free lunchtime lecture focusing on the redesigned space of the Rosalinde and Arthur Gilbert Galleries, which reopened in March 2026. Taking place at the Lydia and Manfred Gorvy Lecture Theatre, the event examines the design processes of the galleries, which remain the only space at the museum dedicated to a private collection. The presentation will highlight key items from the collection alongside their newly designed display formats. Speakers will share curatorial insights and considerations necessary for establishing new narratives regarding craft, collection history, and legacy. The lecture will be delivered by Alice Minter and Jessica Insley, Senior Curator and Curator of the Rosalinde and Arthur Gilbert Collection respectively. While booking is recommended for the lecture series, it is not essential. The museum notes that future courses and events can be followed through the V&A Academy newsletter, and highlights member benefits including free exhibition entry and retail discounts.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Constantinople to Istanbul Exhibition Explores Sixteen Centuries of Art at V&A
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum presents Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition featuring over 200 objects that explore 1,600 years of artistic production across the Byzantine and Ottoman empires.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a comprehensive exhibition titled Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, which runs until 9 May 2027. The exhibition explores 1,600 years of artistic production spanning from AD 330 to 1922. It examines the enduring creative legacy of an imperial capital that shaped the Mediterranean world and beyond, highlighting the distinct yet connected traditions of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires. The display showcases more than 200 objects across four main sections, featuring rare decorative arts, fine silks, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewellery, sculptures, manuscripts, and paintings. The exhibition is organized into four thematic sections: Roman Beginnings, Heaven and Earth, Power and Reach, and Life in the City. The opening section covers the refounding of the city in AD 330 as the capital of the Roman Empire, followed by sections exploring sacred imagery in Christianity, the visual spectacle of Ottoman court authority, and the cosmopolitan rhythms of urban life characterized by diverse languages and faiths. The exhibition concludes by tracing the influence of Byzantine and Ottoman art on 19th-century European culture.

articles.originalTitle: AOM Higher Education/Research: Utah State University Kem & Carolyn Gardner Learning & Leadership Building - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Utah State University Kem and Carolyn Gardner Learning and Leadership Building Wins Award
articles.excerpt: A new academic facility at Utah State University featuring a hybrid steel and mass timber system has received a Mountain States Best Projects Award.
articles.content: Located on the Logan campus of Utah State University, the Kem and Carolyn Gardner Learning and Leadership Building consolidates five academic centers from the Jon M. Huntsman School of Business under one roof. The 44,658-square-foot, three-story academic facility was designed by MHTN Architects, with Jacobsen Construction serving as the general contractor. Inspired by nearby Logan Canyon, the design team incorporated a hybrid steel and mass timber system, making it the university's first mass timber building. Exposed glulam columns and cross-laminated timber decking created a light-filled interior. The mass timber structure also supports the university's goal of achieving carbon neutrality by 2040. Reaching the project site required navigating through two active construction sites near Highway 89, demanding close coordination among all teams. During design development, structural, mechanical, and electrical systems were integrated into cavities to conceal conduits and ductwork while preserving the visual continuity of the timber.

articles.originalTitle: David and Sybil Yurman Are Getting the Museum Treatment in Paris - WWD
articles.title: Paris Musée des Arts Décoratifs to Host David and Sybil Yurman Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The Musée des Arts Décoratifs in Paris announced the first museum exhibition dedicated to the works of painter Sybil Yurman and sculptor David Yurman. Opening in September, the show features over 400 pieces.
articles.content: The Musée des Arts Décoratifs in Paris announced that it will present the first exhibition dedicated to American artist couple David and Sybil Yurman. Curated by Thierry-Maxime Loriot and Matthieu Rousset-Perier, the exhibition is scheduled to open on September 27 and run until February 6, 2028, in the Rivoli gallery on the third floor of the museum. Rooted in the artistic and social movements of the 1960s and 1970s, the showcase highlights their shared practice bridging fine art and craft. Spread across seven spaces, the presentation will include more than 400 works, comprising sculptural jewelry, paintings, sculptures, drawings, photographs, and archival documents. The display also features pieces by Theodore Roszak and Jacques Lipchitz, with whom David Yurman previously apprenticed. The artistic partnership and marriage spanning over five decades has previously been documented through various publications and museum events.

articles.originalTitle: Construction Starts on $246M Niagara Falls Power Station Hotel Conversion - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Historic Niagara Falls Power Station Converted Into Luxury Hotel
articles.excerpt: Construction has begun on a privately financed redevelopment exceeding 246 million dollars to convert the century-old Toronto Power Generating Station near Niagara Falls into a hotel and visitor complex, with completion expected in 2029.
articles.content: Construction has commenced on a redevelopment exceeding 246 million dollars to transform the century-old Toronto Power Generating Station overlooking Niagara Falls into a hotel and visitor complex. Owned by the Ontario provincial agency Niagara Parks, the historic facility is being redeveloped by Toronto Power Hotel Inc., a partnership overseeing the privately financed project. Deltera Contracting Inc. serves as the general contractor, with +VG Architects and MT Planners on the project team. Designed by E.J. Lennox, the steel-frame building opened in 1906 and operated until 1974. The preservation effort will maintain key architectural features while adding a five-star hotel, multiple restaurants, a wellness spa, event facilities, an art gallery, a museum, and public viewing areas. Audited financial statements indicate that approximately 6.72 million dollars in stabilization obligations were transferred to Society Land Holdings Inc. under a long-term lease. Substantial construction completion is anticipated in 2029, with the hotel opening scheduled for 2030.

articles.originalTitle: Building a Permanent Home for a Space Shuttle Was an Engineering Endeavor - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: New Permanent Home Unveiled for Space Shuttle Endeavour in Los Angeles
articles.excerpt: The $450-million Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center at the California Science Center opened its doors to house Endeavour, the only space shuttle exhibited in launch position.
articles.content: The 200,000-sq-ft Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center within the California Science Center was unveiled on Nov. 13. Valued at $450 million, the new facility houses Endeavour, which completed its final mission in June 2011 and remains the only space shuttle exhibited in launch position. ZGF Architects, MATT Construction and engineering teams designed a 200-ft-tall curvilinear stainless-steel structure around the shuttle stack. Project director Dennis R. Jenkins noted that seismic analysis was the most complex aspect of the build, requiring civil and aerospace engineers to coordinate closely to protect the $2-billion NASA-valued orbiter. Safety protocols required workers to secure tools and fasteners with lanyards to prevent damage to the fragile thermal silica tiles. According to Arup, the perimeter diagrid system handles gravity, wind and seismic loads, while six triple-friction pendulum isolator bearings separate the foundation. The center's height was restricted to 200 ft, with the structure built 25 ft below grade to preserve sightlines across Exposition Park.

articles.originalTitle: Miami Beach: Highlights - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach 2026 Gathers the International Art World
articles.excerpt: Held at the cultural crossroads of the Americas from December 4 to 6, 2026, Art Basel Miami Beach unites leading figures in modern and contemporary art with digital art projects and discussions.
articles.content: Situated at the cultural crossroads of the Americas, Art Basel Miami Beach prepares to unite the international art world from December 4 to 6, 2026. The region's leading art fair brings together established galleries, emerging talent, and daring new presentations, spanning Modern masterpieces, contemporary trailblazers, and new frontiers in digital art. The fair's digital art platform, Zero 10, returns with Generation, its largest presentation to date, curated by Karen Archey and Eli Scheinman. Spanning 19 projects, the exhibition explores connections between digital technologies and traditional art forms through works by Sarah Meyohas, Jon Rafman, and Studio DRIFT. Refik Anadol's collaboration with the Yawanawá community transforms Amazonian artwork and weather data into digital imagery, while Harm van den Dorpel's work draws on historical geometric drawings. The Conversations talks program features discussions on patronage, the art market, and the intersection of art and technology. Panels include appearances by Jeff Koons, Julie Mehretu, Kevin Love, Crystal Dunn, Keith Rivers, and Swizz Beatz, with all sessions free and open to the public.

articles.originalTitle: Eight Dead, 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Next to Construction Site - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Eight Dead and 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Near Construction Site
articles.excerpt: An adjoining 96-year-old three-story building collapsed into an excavation site in Brooklyn, New York, leaving 8 people dead and 18 injured. Authorities have launched multiple investigations into the incident.
articles.content: On November 11, a three-story building collapsed into an adjoining excavation site in the Brooklyn borough of New York, resulting in 8 fatalities and 18 injuries. Officials confirmed the dead included two children and two construction workers, while the Fire Department concluded rescue operations on November 12. City records list Townhouse Builders as the general contractor for the project at 2625 Bedford Ave. A project geotechnical report had warned that abutting structures required underpinning and that construction-related vibrations could adversely affect neighboring properties. A March 5 preconstruction survey documented visible cracking at 1321 Flatbush Ave., rating its north masonry facade as poor and its other facades as fair. Area residents reported feeling heavy impacts and shaking while construction was underway next door. Mayor Zohran Mamdani ordered safety inspections at approximately 100 other construction sites linked to companies involved in the project. New York Attorney General Letitia James stated that the Buildings Department would conduct a full investigation, alongside a separate probe launched by Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez. The exact cause of the structural collapse remains undetermined pending the conclusion of ongoing investigations by municipal authorities.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | TAREK EL-ARISS | Emptying the Jars of War, or How We Learned to Love Nature - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Tarek El-Ariss to Discuss War, Nature, and Water Politics at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Tarek El-Ariss will examine how crises alter perceptions of nature and reframe sustainability during a lecture at Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Tarek El-Ariss is scheduled to speak at an event during Biennale Arte 2026 on November 21, 2026. Taking place at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale from 16:00 to 17:30, the lecture will be introduced and moderated by Rasha Salti. The session addresses how crises and wars not only damage the environment but also unsettle perceptions of nature. Drawing from everyday scenes such as saving water jars for bathing during wartime in Lebanon, the discussion traces longer histories and mythologies of water and greenery from the Garden of Eden to Greek and Islamic traditions, while focusing on the oasis as a recurring fantasy. The lecture posits that environmental practices do not necessarily emerge from ethical choices, often arising instead through habit, fear, or the quest for survival. Sustainability is reframed as a negotiation that interrogates the politics of purity and control to imagine alternative futures. Admission to the event is free until venue capacity is reached.
